subject: DPA: transient cache / tombstone retention and certified deletion proof
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@arkadia.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Graham Lee <graham.lee@arkadia.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: transient cache / tombstone retention and certified deletion proof

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Our legal team asked for some clarifications before we move forward with the DPA redlines:

- Can you confirm the retention window for transient caches (prefix/KV caches, ephemeral inference cache) — our initial ask is that any cache which may contain customer PII be purged within 24 hours; your DPA draft currently lists 90 days for logs and 30 days for temporary artifacts and we need to understand the practical surface area.
- For deletion requests, Arkadia needs a certified deletion proof for PII erasures. Do you provide a signed proof (audit manifest) that includes the keys/tombstone IDs removed + timestamp? What is the SLA for producing that evidence?
- If you rely on snapshots/backups, what carve-outs apply for onshore copies and backups (we operate primarily in US, but need to know any cross-border replication windows)?

Attached are the in-house redlines from our counsel (high-level). If Redwood can propose firm language for (1) transient cache TTL, (2) certified deletion mechanism, and (3) an onshore-only backup carve-out or escalation path, that will help us move quickly.

Sonia
Sonia Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Arkadia Health

<Attachment: arkadia_dpa_redlines_excerpt.pdf>

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@arkadia.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 13:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: transient cache / tombstone retention and certified deletion proof

Sonia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Camila (security) and Marissa (legal ops) so we can give concrete language and an operations plan. High-level response below, we can formalize a redline in the attached counter: Redwood_DPA_counter_v1.docx.

1) Transient caches: Our runtime distinguishes between (a) ephemeral inference KV / prefix caches (used only during a single inference session) and (b) short-term cross-request caches used for batching/throughput optimizations. For PII, we recommend and can commit to a 48-hour max TTL on any cache that can contain customer-supplied PII. System logs that contain telemetry only (no PII) will remain at 90 days by default; we can scope that.

2) Certified deletion evidence: We can provide a signed deletion manifest. Proposed mechanics: when a deletion request is processed for a tenant, the system emits a manifest listing tombstone IDs + object digests + deletion timestamps. The manifest is signed by Redwood's KMS-wrapped key and stored in a tamper-evident audit log. We can produce that manifest on request within 72 hours; in high-priority lawful requests we can expedite to 48 hours for PII (contractually).

3) Backups & onshore carve-outs: We do take periodic snapshots for disaster recovery. For Arkadia we can offer an onshore-only backup region (US) and restrict cross-border replication unless explicitly requested. We can also add a clause requiring Redwood to notify Arkadia 10 days before any cross-border restore that would result in data leaving the onshore region.

Camila / Marissa — can you confirm the deletion manifest format (sample manifest in evidence_matrix_template.xlsx) and the legal language to propose for the DPA? Sonia — if that aligns, I'll upload a redline with the proposed 48-hour/72-hour commitments and the manifest wording.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

<Attachment: Redwood_DPA_counter_v1.docx>

From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@arkadia.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Graham Lee <graham.lee@arkadia.com>, legal@arkadia.com
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: transient cache / tombstone retention and certified deletion proof

Michael — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from our counsel after reviewing the proposed approach:

- 48 hours for transient PII caches is closer to acceptable than 90 days; counsel wants 'maximum 48 hours' explicitly in the DPA with an exception only for system debugging where Arkadia signs off in writing.
- For the deletion manifest, the legal team requires that the manifest includes (i) tenant identifier, (ii) canonical object IDs, (iii) hash digests, (iv) deletion operation id, (v) the KMS key id used to sign the manifest, and (vi) a signed timestamp. Can you confirm those fields will be present?
- Counsel wants an SLA for delivery of the manifest of 48 hours for PII deletions. They also asked for a Bermuda clause: if Redwood is unable to provide the manifest within the SLA, Arkadia may require Redwood to engage a mutually agreed third-party auditor at Redwood's expense to certify the deletion.

I'll attach the sections we want to see changed. If you can accept the manifest fields and 48-hour SLA for both deletion and proof, we can move to DocuSign. Otherwise, we need to keep negotiating.

Sonia

Team — forwarding Arkadia's follow-up. They are firm on the 48-hour SLA for both deletion and deletion proof and want specific manifest fields plus a third-party audit fallback. I propose the following operational acceptance and legal compromise:

Operational proposal (for Camila to validate):
- Implement a manifest payload that includes tenant_id, object_id(s), SHA256 digest(s), deletion_operation_id, kms_key_id, and RFC3339 signed timestamp. Store the manifest in an append-only audit bucket with bucket-level logging enabled.
- For PII deletions triggered via the DPA process, we commit to producing the manifest within 48 hours. For non-PII deletions, SLA is 72 hours.
- If Redwood fails the SLA, we accept the contract language requiring a mutually agreed third-party auditor; Redwood reserves the right to cure or provide remediation before auditor engagement but accepts auditor cost responsibility after a second SLA miss.

Legal language suggestion (for Marissa):
- "Redwood shall purge customer-designated personal data from ephemeral caches within 48 hours of receipt of a valid deletion request, except where Customer expressly consents in writing to a longer debug window. Redwood will provide a signed deletion manifest that contains tenant identifier, canonical object identifiers, cryptographic digests, deletion operation identifier, the KMS key identifier used to produce the signature, and a signed timestamp. Redwood shall deliver the manifest within 48 hours for personal data deletions and within 72 hours for non-personal data deletions. If Redwood fails to deliver within the SLA on two (2) consecutive occasions, Customer may require Redwood to commission a mutually agreed third-party attestation at Redwoodâs expense."
Camila — can you confirm we can produce the signed manifest as described and that the append-only bucket + KMS signature satisfies tamper-evidence? Also point me to the sample manifest in the Drive link and confirm whether we should offer 48h expedited request handling as a paid SLA (or include as part of the enterprise commitment).

Marissa — can you draft the redline above into the DPA and I'll send a final to Sonia if Camila confirms ops.

Thanks,

Michael
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
